title: Quinn Scheider
text: My name is Quinn Scheider, and I’m currently a Masters of Data Science student at The University of British Columbia Vancouver.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text: My first few weeks here have been a lot of fun but also difficult at times as I’ve moved to a new country. Understanding how certain things work here in Vancouver when compared to things in Minnesota has been fun and interesting to experience. Especially since I drove my own car here, there are lots of new things to experience. Bike lanes are not as popular in Minnesota as here in Vancouver, so I’ve had to make sure everytime I turn onto a new street I don’t hit a bicyclist riding by. Other than that I’ve done plenty of hikes and experienced all throughout Squamish and Whistler which has been a blast.

title: About
text: I just graduated from my undergrad in May of 2026 from Saint John’s University with a major in Mathematics. During undergrad I played on the Saint John’s Men’s Volleyball team where I was selected as a Captain my Junior and Senior year. I’ve had two different internships during undergrad, working as a HRIS Analyst for Delta Airlines and a Data Engineer at Commscope, where I grew my pashion for the field of Data Science and Data Engineering. In my freetime I love to go mountaineering, splitboarding/ski touring, climbing, and working out/running. I’m originally from Minnesota in the United States, and I’m also a EU Blue Card eligible citizen. I’m not 100% sure where I’d like to live after finishing the MDS program at UBC but I hope to move to a place where I can continue my pashion for mountaineering and splitboarding to help me keep a solid worklife balance in my future. As a U.S. citizen with a EU Blue card the easiest places for me to move would obviously be in the U.S. or a EU country but I’m also open to living somewhere in Canada!

title: Python Penguin Analysis
section: Ploting the body mass and flipper length grouped by each penguin type
text:
Ploting the body mass and flipper length grouped by each penguin type

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))

colors = {
    "Adelie": "#1f77b4",
    "Chinstrap": "#ff7f0e",
    "Gentoo": "#2ca02c",
}

for species, species_data in penguins_clean.groupby(
    "species",
    observed=True,
):
    ax.scatter(
        species_data["flipper_length_mm"],
        species_data["body_mass_g"],
        label=species,
        color=colors[species],
        alpha=0.7,
    )

ax.set_title("Penguin body mass and flipper length")
ax.set_xlabel("Flipper length (mm)")
ax.set_ylabel("Body mass (g)")
ax.legend(title="Species")
ax.grid(alpha=0.2)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Body mass and flipper length for the three Palmer Penguin species.

title: R Penguin Analysis

Loading and prepping the data

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(palmerpenguins)

penguins_clean <- penguins |>
  filter(
    !is.na(species),
    !is.na(bill_length_mm),
    !is.na(bill_depth_mm),
    !is.na(sex)
  )

title: R Penguin Analysis
text:
Plotting the bill length

ggplot(
  penguins_clean,
  aes(
    x = bill_length_mm,
    y = bill_depth_mm,
    colour = species,
    shape = sex
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.75, size = 2.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Penguin bill dimensions vary by species",
    x = "Bill length (mm)",
    y = "Bill depth (mm)",
    colour = "Species",
    shape = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()







Figure 1: Bill length and bill depth by Palmer Penguin species and sex.
